$comment: The frozen scenario the eligibility proof fixtures are built from.
Consumed by `npm run fixtures:eligibility` (which proves) and by
packages/contracts/test/EligibilityVerifier.test.cjs (which deploys a
tender with these exact values). Two implementations reading one spec is
what makes the test a cross-check rather than a tautology.
The bidding window uses far-future absolute timestamps on purpose. A
fixture anchored to 'now' passes the day it is generated and fails every
day after, and the failure looks like a broken verifier rather than a
stale fixture.
The scenario is the whitepaper Figure 5 dataset: a BDT 50 crore turnover
floor, five years of relevant experience, certification 9001.

credentialEpoch is 7, not 1, so the fixture's published registry and revocation roots cannot be overwritten by the lifecycle e2e test, which uses epoch 1. Both write to issuerRegistryRoot[epoch]; sharing an epoch would make a previously valid proof stop verifying for reasons unrelated to the proof.
reviewWindow is 300 to match the deployment's default policy floor, so the same fixture activates on the live chain as well as in unit tests.
The identity records are SYNTHETIC. No real company's registration, trade licence or VAT/BIN appears anywhere in this repository.
TEST MATERIAL ONLY. A deterministic 3-of-5 Feldman dealing, so the
committed fixture can carry a sealed ciphertext that the opening tests
can actually open. The secret and the member shares are published here
on purpose: a reproducible opening test needs them, and a tender whose
shares are in a public git repository is obviously not a real tender.
NEVER reuse these values for anything that matters.
The revocation tree the tender's deadline root is pinned from.
A DIFFERENT credential is revoked in it (9999, not either bidder's), so
the deadline root differs from the submission-time root while both
bidders remain unrevoked. If the two roots were equal the original
eligibility proof would double as a status proof and the close-time check
would be exercised only vacuously.
